prs.title: fix: buffer stdio server writes during progress notifications
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both modify the write stream buffer size in stdio_server — #2215 makes it a configurable parameter (defaulting to 0), while #2654 hardcodes it to 1 to fix a specific deadlock when a progress notification is mid-flush and the handler tries to enqueue its final response. They diff the same line and conflict at merge time. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both modify the write stream buffer size in stdio_server — #2215 makes it a configurable parameter (defaulting to 0), while #2654 hardcodes it to 1 to fix a specific deadlock when a progress notification is mid-flush and the handler tries to enqueue its final response. They diff the same line and conflict at merge time. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #2654 fixes a concrete, reproducible bug (handler blocked enqueuing final response while stdout_writer flushes a progress notification) and includes a BlockingStdout test that proves the failure mode. #2215 defaults write_stream_buffer_size=0, so it ships the same bug unless callers explicitly pass write_stream_buffer_size=1 — shifting the burden to users who may not know the right value. #2654's single-line targeted fix with test coverage is more immediately correct; the configurability from #2215 can be layered on top later if needed.

prs.cluster_pick_reason: PR #2777 removes the redundant `{e}` interpolation from the message string (e.g., `"Invalid registration response"` instead of `f"Invalid registration response: {e}"`), so the original exception appears only once via the chained `__cause__` rather than duplicated in both the message and the traceback chain. PR #2565 applies `from e` to the same sites but retains the f-string interpolation, leaving the original exception text redundantly printed twice.

prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: KeyboardInterrupt traceback leaks from MCPServer.run() across all transports — both add an identical try/except KeyboardInterrupt: return around the match transport block in server.py (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: PR #2778 makes only the targeted try/except change; PR #2745 additionally removes `# pragma: no cover` from the sse branch and changes the streamable-http pragma to `# pragma: no branch`, mixing unrelated coverage-annotation edits into the bug fix. clusters.pick_reason: #2654 fixes a concrete, reproducible bug (handler blocked enqueuing final response while stdout_writer flushes a progress notification) and includes a BlockingStdout test that proves the failure mode. #2215 defaults write_stream_buffer_size=0, so it ships the same bug unless callers explicitly pass write_stream_buffer_size=1 — shifting the burden to users who may not know the right value. #2654's single-line targeted fix with test coverage is more immediately correct; the configurability from #2215 can be layered on top later if needed.

members.author: yaowubarbara
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2654: Both modify the write stream buffer size in stdio_server — #2215 makes it a configurable parameter (defaulting to 0), while #2654 hardcodes it to 1 to fix a specific deadlock when a progress notification is mid-flush and the handler tries to enqueue its final response. They diff the same line and conflict at merge time.
